transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I keep hearing people talking about me. It’s usually the board members or my staff, and they’re always saying I’m ruining the company. I hear them right through the conference room walls. Which, by the way, are made of this imported frosted glass we had installed last year. It cost an absolute fortune, but the contractor was just a complete nightmare to deal with. He kept delaying the project because of some shipping issue from Italy, and his communication was just awful, always making excuses. 

But anyway, I hear them talking through those walls, or even coming from my phone when it’s completely turned off. I just got this phone, actually, the new titanium one, though honestly the battery life is so much worse than my old one. I feel like I have to charge it twice a day, and the charger cable it came with is ridiculously short. 

But their voices... they sound so incredibly clear that I actually answer them out loud. I'll just start talking back, defending my decisions to the room, before I even realize no one else around me heard a thing. So... yes, that's why I'm here.
Do you experience any other sensations, like seeing or feeling things that aren't there, besides hearing these voices?

No, I haven't seen anything... or felt anything weird like that. It's really just the voices. Though, speaking of feeling things, I did have this terrible stiffness in my neck last week. I think it’s from my new office chair. My assistant ordered it—supposed to be this high-end ergonomic mesh thing, but honestly, it’s like sitting on a rock. I told her to get the leather executive one, but she insisted this was better for my posture. She’s always reading these wellness blogs and trying to push them on me. Just last Tuesday she brought in this green juice that smelled like lawn clippings. I mean, I appreciate that she cares, but I’m running a company, I don't have time to drink algae. But no, to answer your question, no visions or anything like that. Just the voices.
Do the voices you hear ever talk about what you're thinking, or are they mainly discussing your actions or decisions at work?

No, they don't... I haven't heard them say anything about what's actually in my head. I don't think they know what I'm thinking. It's really just them criticizing my decisions. Like yesterday, they were going on and on about the Q3 budget cuts. 

Which, honestly, I had to make because our marketing department is just bleeding money right now. I hired this new director, Greg, and I swear, his first day he shows up in these absolutely hideous tasseled loafers. I mean, who wears tassels to a modern corporate office? We have a very specific aesthetic. I paid this designer, Elise, an absolute fortune to make the space look sleek—lots of chrome and monochrome tones. She actually tried to push these velvet accent chairs for the lobby. Velvet! Can you imagine? One spilled latte and it's ruined forever. And people are so careless with their coffee. The barista at the place downstairs always burns the milk anyway, so it tastes terrible, but people still buy it. I usually just get a black Americano now, but it gives me heartburn if I drink it too fast. 

But I told Greg he needs to get his team in order because... wait, what was I saying? Did you ask about the marketing budget?
Do the voices you hear ever tell you to do something or take a specific action?

No, no, they don't give me orders or tell me to do things. They just talk *about* me. Like I was telling you, I hear them through those frosted glass walls or coming out of my phone when it's completely powered down. It's always the board members or my staff, just going on and on about how I'm ruining the company. And it's so incredibly clear, I literally start answering them out loud, defending myself, before I realize the room is empty and nobody else heard a thing. 

Speaking of the board, though... Arthur, the chairman, he's been insisting we host the annual retreat in Aspen this year. Aspen! In November! Does he have any idea how unpredictable the weather is? Last time I went skiing in November, I got stranded in Denver for two days because of a blizzard. The airport hotel was a disaster—the heating in my room was broken, and they only gave me this thin, scratchy wool blanket. I'm actually allergic to wool, it makes my skin break out in these terrible red patches. I had to use this special hydrocortisone cream for a week, and it completely ruined my silk blouses because the cream is so greasy. Silk is so high-maintenance anyway, you have to dry clean it, and my usual dry cleaner just retired. He moved to Florida, near Boca, I think. His son took over the shop, but he uses this new eco-friendly solvent that leaves a weird smell. 

But no, the voices don't tell me what to do. They just criticize me and say I'm ruining everything.
Do the voices you hear seem to happen more often when you're under a lot of stress at work?

I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. I don't think it's just when I'm stressed, because they just seem to talk whenever they want to. But then again, when am I not stressed? I'm running an entire company. 

Like, just yesterday, the catering company completely botched the order for the executive luncheon. I explicitly told them we had three gluten-free board members and two vegans. And what do they send? A massive tray of chicken parmesan and garlic bread. Garlic bread! In a closed boardroom! The smell just lingers in the upholstery for days. We have these beautiful custom drapes in there, imported from Italy. They cost an absolute fortune, and you can't just spray cheap air freshener on them. You have to get this specialized steaming service to come in, and the guy who does it, Hector, he's always running late. Last time he kept me waiting for two hours, and I had to reschedule my massage. I get deep tissue because I carry all my tension in my shoulders, right between my shoulder blades. My massage therapist says I have the tightest muscles she's ever seen. She uses this lavender oil that's supposed to be calming, but honestly, it just reminds me of my grandmother's guest bathroom. 

But, um, what was the question? Oh, the stress. No, I don't really know if the voices care about my stress levels. I haven't really tracked it.
Are the voices you hear something that happens all the time, or do they come and go?

They... well, they happen a lot. I'd say they're pretty constant. Like I mentioned, that's actually why I came in to see you. I just keep hearing them talking about me, saying I'm ruining the company, and it's always coming through the conference room walls, or even my phone when it's completely shut off. And it's so clear, I literally start talking back to them before I realize the room is empty. 

It's just exhausting because I'm trying to run a business, and my phone is already such a distraction. I actually upgraded to the newest model last month because the battery on my old one was draining so fast. But honestly, the new camera on this one is terrible. It makes everything look so washed out. I tried taking a picture of this beautiful orchid someone sent me for my birthday—it was a Phalaenopsis, stunning, with these deep purple spots—but the photo looked completely gray. I have this perfect spot for it on my credenza, right where it gets the morning light. Though the cleaning staff keeps moving it when they dust. I've told them a hundred times not to touch my plants. The last time they watered my peace lily, they completely drowned it. The leaves turned yellow and just fell off. It's impossible to find good help these days. I tried using a new agency, but the woman they sent didn't even know how to use a microfiber cloth properly. 

But anyway, yeah, the voices... they don't really go away. They're just always there, criticizing me.
How do you feel when you hear these voices talking about you?

Well, I... I don't know exactly how I feel. I mean, they're always criticizing me, so I guess it makes me feel... defensive? Frustrated? I just want them to stop. 

But honestly, the frustration is nothing compared to how I felt when my assistant booked me on a commercial flight last week. Commercial! I specifically told her to charter a plane for the Chicago trip because I needed to review the quarterly financials in private. But no, she booked me in first class on a regular airline. And let me tell you, "first class" is a joke these days. The seat barely reclined, and the woman next to me kept taking off her shoes. Who does that on an airplane? It's completely unsanitary. The flight attendant didn't even say anything to her. I tried to complain, but the attendant was too busy passing out those tiny bags of pretzels. I can't eat pretzels anyway, the salt makes me retain water, and I had a photoshoot for a magazine profile the next day. They were doing a whole spread on female executives, and they hired this makeup artist who used the heaviest foundation. It felt like I was wearing a mask. I had to scrub my face for twenty minutes that night just to get it off, and I ended up breaking out right on my chin. 

So, um... yeah. I don't really know how I feel about the voices. Just... annoyed, I guess.
Do you ever hear the voices when you are completely alone and not thinking about work?

Well, yes, even when I'm alone. I mean, that's exactly why I made this appointment. I keep hearing them—the board members, sometimes the staff—talking about me, saying I'm completely ruining the company. And it happens when I'm just sitting by myself, not even thinking about the quarterly reports or anything. It comes right through the conference room walls, or... or even my phone. My phone will be completely shut off, sitting on the marble counter in my kitchen, and I still hear them. It's so clear that I'll actually start answering them out loud before I realize nobody else is there. 

Which is just... it's so frustrating because that marble counter was a nightmare to install. I had to have it shipped directly from Carrara, Italy, and the contractors scratched the edge when they were carrying it in. I told the foreman, I said, "Do you have any idea how much this slab cost?" And he just gave me this blank look, like he didn't even care. Nobody takes pride in their work anymore. I had to hire a completely different specialist to come in and polish out the scratch, and he tracked mud all over my Persian rug. It's a silk blend, completely irreplaceable, hand-woven in Iran. I had to send it out to be professionally cleaned, and it was gone for three weeks. My living room felt completely bare without it. I tried putting down this temporary wool runner, but it just clashed horribly with the custom sofa I had upholstered in this beautiful seafoam velvet. 

But, yes, to answer your question... even when I'm alone and trying to relax, I still hear them saying I'm ruining everything.
Do you think the voices you hear are coming from real people or from somewhere else?

Well, of course they're real people. I mean, like I've been saying since I came in here, it's usually the board members or my staff. I keep hearing them talking about me, saying I'm ruining the company, and it comes right through the conference room walls, or my phone even when it's completely off. It sounds so clear that I literally answer them out loud before I realize no one else heard it. So yes, they are real people. 

The board members are always whispering anyway. Especially Richard. He's always so concerned about the budget, but then he insists we use this ridiculously expensive catering company for our monthly meetings. And let me tell you, the food is atrocious. Last week they brought these blueberry scones that were like eating actual sand. I took one bite and had to discreetly spit it into my napkin. And the napkin was paper! Can you believe that? I specifically mandated linen napkins for the executive suite. It’s about projecting a certain standard. You can’t ask investors for capital and then hand them a flimsy paper towel that dissolves if you spill a single drop of sparkling water. I had to throw the entire pastry platter directly into the trash, which is just a complete waste of company funds. Honestly, if anyone is ruining the company, it's Richard and his dreadful taste in caterers. 

But... what was I saying? Oh, right. Yes, they are definitely real people I'm hearing.
Can you recognize the specific voices of the board members or staff when you hear them talking about you?

Well, yes, I can recognize them. It's usually the board members or my staff. Like I said, I hear them through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it's completely powered down. I hear them so clearly, saying I'm ruining the company, and I know exactly who it is. I'll hear Richard's voice, or Sarah from accounting, and it's so distinct that I literally answer them out loud before I realize nobody else is around. 

Sarah has this very distinct, nasally voice anyway. It's incredibly grating. She always speaks up during the quarterly reviews to complain about the travel budget, which is rich coming from someone who expensed a three-hundred-dollar dinner at a steakhouse last month. I saw the receipt. She tried to claim it was a client dinner, but the client she listed was in London at the time. I know this for a fact because I was supposed to be in London too, but my flight got delayed because of some issue with the landing gear. We sat on the tarmac for four hours. Four hours! And they wouldn't even let us use the lavatory for the first two. The air conditioning was barely working, and the man across the aisle from me was sweating profusely and breathing so loudly. I tried to put on my noise-canceling headphones, but I had left the charging case on my desk, right next to the new crystal paperweight I bought. It's a gorgeous piece, Baccarat crystal, shaped like a lotus flower. It catches the afternoon light perfectly. 

But anyway, yes, I know exactly who is talking. I recognize their voices perfectly when they're saying those awful things about me.
Do you think the voices you hear could be your own thoughts or are they definitely coming from outside yourself?

Well, no, they're definitely from outside. I mean, they aren't my thoughts. Like I've been saying, I hear the board members or the staff through the conference room walls, or coming out of my phone when it's completely off. They're saying I'm ruining the company, and it's so clear that I'll answer them out loud. If it was my own thoughts, I wouldn't be talking back to an empty room, would I? 

It's just so disrespectful. I built this company from the ground up, practically. I remember when our first office was just this tiny, cramped space above a dry cleaner. The smell of the chemicals would seep through the floorboards every afternoon around 3:00 PM. I used to get these terrible migraines from it. I tried buying all these expensive air purifiers, the ones with the HEPA filters and the UV lights that supposedly kill bacteria, but nothing worked. I ended up having to burn these imported soy candles just to mask the scent. They were incredibly expensive, infused with sandalwood and bergamot, poured by hand in this little boutique in Paris. I actually met the artisan who makes them when I was on vacation there five years ago. We had coffee at this charming little café near the Seine. I ordered a cappuccino, but the milk was far too hot—it completely scalded the espresso. It’s impossible to find a decent barista these days, even in Europe. People just don't pay attention to the details anymore. 

But, yes, the voices are definitely coming from the outside. I hear them clear as day.
Can you make the voices stop talking when you want them to?

No, I can't just make them stop. I've tried everything. I mean, they just keep coming through the conference room walls, or right out of my phone when it's completely powered down. It's always the board members or the staff, going on and on about how I'm ruining the company. And it's so clear that I'll just answer them out loud, and then I realize I'm standing there talking to myself. I can't just turn it off. 

I tried turning off my phone, obviously, but that doesn't work. I even bought a new phone. I got the latest model, the one with the titanium casing. It's supposed to be incredibly durable. The salesperson at the store was so pushy about the extended warranty, though. I hate when they do that. They act like you're going to drop it in a lake the second you walk out the door. I did drop a phone in a lake once, actually. It was Lake Tahoe. We had rented this stunning cabin right on the water for a corporate retreat. The views were breathtaking, but the mosquitoes were absolutely vicious. I had to buy this organic, DEET-free repellent that smelled like citronella and despair. It left this awful sticky residue on everything. I ruined a perfectly good silk blouse because of it. It was a Diane von Furstenberg wrap top, a limited edition print. I was so upset. I tried taking it to my dry cleaner, but they just shrugged and said the oil had set. Dry cleaners are practically useless these days. You pay a premium for what? A plastic bag and a wire hanger? It's insulting. 

But no, I can't make the voices stop. If I could, I wouldn't be sitting here, would I?
Do you think the voices could be a product of your own mind?

No, absolutely not. I mean, how could they be? I've told you, I hear them through the conference room walls, or coming right out of my phone when it's completely powered off. It's the board members, my staff, saying I'm ruining the company. It's so clear, so real, that I actually answer them out loud before I realize nobody else is in the room. If it was just my mind, it wouldn't sound like Richard or Sarah, would it? 

Speaking of my mind, I really need to start taking those omega-3 supplements again. I read this fascinating article in a magazine while I was waiting at the dentist last week. It was about how fish oil is supposed to improve cognitive function and reduce inflammation. Although, I have to say, the waiting room at my dentist's office is just atrocious. They have these awful, stiff leather chairs that squeak every time you shift your weight, and they always play this terrible elevator music. It's like a soft-jazz version of 80s pop hits. Who wants to hear a saxophone cover of 'Careless Whisper' while they're waiting for a root canal? It's completely absurd. I tried to suggest they play classical music instead—maybe some Vivaldi or Chopin—but the receptionist just gave me this blank stare. Receptionists these days have zero initiative. I had an assistant once, maybe five years ago, who was just like that. I'd ask her to book a flight, and she'd somehow manage to book it for the wrong month. The wrong month! I almost missed a crucial merger meeting in Chicago because of her. Chicago is dreadful in the winter, by the way. The wind literally cuts through your coat. I had to buy this ridiculously oversized cashmere scarf just to walk two blocks to the restaurant. 

But no, to answer your question, they aren't my mind making things up. I hear them. They're real.
Do you think the voices could be coming from your own thoughts or memories, rather than from outside yourself?

Well, I thought we just went over this, but no, they are definitely not my own thoughts or memories. I mean, I'm the one who came in because I keep hearing them, right? It's the board members, it's my staff, and they're talking about me through the conference room walls, or coming out of my phone when it's completely off. They're saying I'm ruining the company. It's not a memory. I hear them so clearly that I answer them out loud, and then I realize no one else heard it. 

I don't know why people have such a hard time understanding how acoustics work. I had this contractor once, when we were remodeling the executive suite, who tried to tell me that the drywall we were using was soundproof. Soundproof! I laughed in his face. I said, "Listen, if I can hear the intern microwaving leftover fish in the breakroom, this wall is not soundproof." It's incredibly unprofessional to microwave fish in a shared office space, by the way. I had to send out a company-wide memo about it. We had this one girl, an intern from some liberal arts college, who brought in salmon every single Tuesday. She always wore these oversized, chunky knit sweaters that looked like they were made out of recycled bath mats. I don't understand fashion these days. It's like everyone is trying to look as unkempt as possible. I always wear a tailored blazer. It projects authority. You need authority when you're running a company, especially when your own board is constantly whispering about you through the walls. 

So, no, they aren't my thoughts. They're real people, saying real things, and I hear them.
Have you experienced any traumatic events in your past?

Traumatic? No, I wouldn't say so. I've had a very standard, successful life, really. I mean, unless you count the time we hosted the global summit in 2018. That was a complete nightmare. We had booked the grand ballroom at the Plaza, and the event coordinator—this incredibly high-strung woman named Chloe—somehow double-booked the coat check staff. It was an absolute disaster. It started sleeting halfway through the evening, and suddenly we had three hundred executives trying to retrieve their cashmere overcoats from one terrified teenager. 

I actually had to step in and organize the queue myself. I was wearing these stunning Jimmy Choo stilettos, the ones with the subtle crystal detailing on the heel. They are beautiful, but they are absolutely not meant for standing on marble floors for two hours. My feet were throbbing for a week. I tried to get a massage at that high-end spa downtown to recover, but the masseuse kept trying to talk to me about her chakras. I am paying for deep tissue, not a spiritual awakening, you know? It's like people have completely forgotten how to just provide a service. You go into a coffee shop now, and they want to know your name, your weekend plans, your zodiac sign. Just hand me the espresso! I drink it black. Anything else is just masking the flavor of a poor-quality roast. I buy my beans directly from a small farm in Colombia now. 

But no, to answer your question, no actual trauma in my past. Just... incompetent people everywhere.
Do you ever criticize yourself in the same way that the voices do?

Criticize myself? Why would I do that? I'm the one holding this entire operation together. No, the criticism is entirely external. Like I keep saying—and I really don't know how to make this any clearer—I hear them. The board members, my staff, they're the ones saying I'm ruining the company. I hear them talking about me through the conference room walls, or coming out of my phone when it's completely powered down. It's so distinct, so incredibly clear, that I'll actually answer them out loud. And then I sit there and realize no one else in the room heard a thing. 

It's infuriating, honestly. Almost as infuriating as the new smart-home system I had installed last month. The contractor promised me it would be seamless, completely integrated. "You can control the thermostat with your voice," he said. Well, yesterday I told it to lower the temperature to 68 degrees, and it turned on the sprinklers in the front yard. The sprinklers! It was pouring rain outside anyway. I had to stand on the porch in my silk bathrobe trying to manually override the control panel while the delivery guy from FedEx just stared at me. He was dropping off a package of those Colombian coffee beans I mentioned earlier. The packaging they use is so excessive, by the way. It comes in a box, inside another box, wrapped in this crinkly brown paper that gets everywhere. I appreciate protecting the product, but it's like opening a Russian nesting doll just to get my morning espresso. I actually wrote a very sternly worded email to their customer service department about their packaging waste. Not that anyone reads emails anymore. Everyone just wants to communicate via Slack or text message. It's impossible to maintain a professional tone with emojis. 

But no, I don't criticize myself. It's them. I hear them through the walls.
Do you think the voices you hear might be reflecting any of your own concerns or fears about your performance at work?

Fears? No, absolutely not. I don't have concerns about my performance. I built this company from the ground up, I know exactly what I'm doing. If anyone has performance issues, it's the staff. We just went through quarterly reviews, and I had to sit through a presentation by my VP of Marketing, Greg, who insists on using these horrific pie charts. I literally had to stop him and say that nobody is going to take our Q3 projections seriously if his slides look like a 1970s bowling alley. He used this awful mustard yellow and burnt orange color scheme. It was physically painful to look at.

I actually used to bowl, you know, just briefly in my twenties before I left college to start the business. We had these custom silk-blend shirts made. Real embroidery. You can't find good embroidery anymore. I took a set of Egyptian cotton towels to get monogrammed last month—the really plush ones, 1000-thread-count—and the woman at the boutique tried to tell me they only do heat-transfer vinyl now. Vinyl! On luxury linens! I just turned around and walked right out the door. It’s like no one cares about craftsmanship anymore. You buy a car today, and the dashboard is just one giant touchscreen. I miss the tactile feel of real buttons. My first car had this beautiful walnut wood trim on the steering wheel, and it just felt so substantial in your hands. 

But no, I'm not worried about my performance at all. I'm doing a stellar job, they're just ungrateful.
Do you believe the voices you hear are the actual board members and staff, or do you think they might be impersonating them?

Impersonating them? No, no, it's definitely them. I know their voices. I mean, I hired most of them, didn't I? I hear them clear as day, right through the conference room walls, or—like I said—coming out of my phone when it's completely powered down. They're always saying the same things, that I'm ruining the company, that I don't know what I'm doing. It's so incredibly distinct that I'll literally answer them out loud. I'll be sitting there in my office, and I'll just say, "Excuse me, I can hear you," and then I realize the room is completely empty and no one else heard a thing. 

It's just like when I try to get a straight answer out of my interior designer, Marcus. I hired him to redo the executive suites, and I specifically asked for a minimalist aesthetic with cool tones. Slate grays, maybe a touch of navy. Do you know what he brought me? Swatches of mauve. Mauve! It's like a dusty purple from a 1980s waiting room. I told him, "Marcus, if I wanted my office to look like a discount dentist's lobby, I would have gone to a flea market." And he had the nerve to tell me that mauve is making a comeback. A comeback! Just like those high-waisted jeans everyone is wearing now. I tried a pair on at a boutique in SoHo last week, and I swear, the zipper went all the way up to my ribcage. Who finds that comfortable? You can't even sit down in them without feeling like you're being cut in half. I ended up just buying a cashmere wrap instead. You can never have too much cashmere, really. Though the dry cleaning bills are astronomical. My cleaner, Mr. Chen, he does a fabulous job, but he insists on using these wire hangers that just ruin the shoulders of my garments. I've told him a hundred times to use the velvet ones I provide, but he just smiles and nods and then—wire hangers. 

But yes, it's definitely the board members and the staff. I hear them talking about me ruining the company, and I answer them before I even realize they aren't actually in the room with me. It's them. I know it is.
Do you think the voices you hear might be saying things that you, yourself, are afraid to admit or worry about?

Afraid to admit? No, I'm not afraid to admit anything. I'm a very straightforward person. That's why I'm here, actually. I came in because I keep hearing them—the board members, the staff—talking about me through the conference room walls, or from my phone even when it's completely off. They're always saying I'm ruining the company. And it sounds so incredibly clear that I answer them out loud before I even realize no one else heard it. 

It’s just like when I’m trying to order a simple salad at that new bistro downtown. You go in, and you just want a nice Niçoise, maybe some seared tuna, and they hand you a menu on an iPad. I don’t want to scroll through a digital interface to choose my dressing. And half the time, the screen is smudged with someone else's fingerprints. It’s incredibly unsanitary. I actually carry these little individually wrapped antibacterial wipes in my purse now. The lavender-scented ones. Though, honestly, the lavender is a bit overpowering. It smells less like a French countryside and more like a discount potpourri sachet you'd find in a grandmother's guest bathroom. I bought a real lavender plant for my kitchen windowsill hoping it would be better, but I think I overwatered it. Or maybe it didn't get enough sun? The lighting in my kitchen is very tricky. I had these imported Italian pendant lights installed, hand-blown glass, absolutely gorgeous, but the bulbs they require are nearly impossible to find. I had to order them from a specialty supplier in Milan, and they took six weeks to arrive. Six weeks! And when they finally got here, the delivery driver left the box right on the edge of the porch where it could have easily been knocked over by a stray cat. 

But no, I'm not worried about what they're saying. I just wish they would stop talking about me ruining the company when my phone is off.
Do you think the voices might be echoing any criticisms you have of yourself?

Criticisms of myself? No, I don't know why we keep going in circles about this. I'm not criticizing myself. Like I just explained to you, it's *them*. It's the board members and the staff. I hear them through the conference room walls, or coming out of my phone when it is completely powered down and sitting on my desk. They are the ones saying I’m ruining the company, not me. It sounds so real that I literally answer them out loud before I even realize the room is empty and nobody else heard it. 

I don't have time to sit around criticizing myself, I'm too busy trying to manage people who can't follow basic instructions. Take my assistant, Chloe, for example. I sent her out this morning to get me a simple iced matcha latte. I specifically said almond milk, light ice. She comes back twenty minutes later with oat milk. Oat milk! It tastes like liquid cardboard. I do not understand this obsession everyone has with oats right now. Overnight oats, oat milk, oat flour. It's peasant food. 

My grandmother used to feed oats to her horses. She had this stunning equestrian estate in Virginia, and we used to go riding every summer. I had a chestnut mare named Duchess. She was incredibly temperamental—you had to brush her coat exactly the way she liked, with this specific natural-bristle brush, or she'd try to nip at your fingers. I actually still have my custom leather riding boots from back then. They were handmade in Florence. The leather is so supple. It's not like the stiff, synthetic garbage they try to pass off as luxury these days. I went into a high-end boutique last week to look for some ankle boots, and the salesgirl actually tried to sell me "vegan leather." Vegan leather is just polyurethane! It's plastic! They slap a trendy, eco-friendly label on it and charge you eight hundred dollars. It's a complete scam. 

People just don't appreciate authenticity anymore. Which is exactly why I know I'm right about the business, despite what the board keeps whispering through the walls. I hear them clear as day. But no, to answer your question, it's not me criticizing myself. It's definitely them.

But no, I'm not worried about my performance at all. I'm doing a stellar job, they're just ungrateful.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a delusional disorder
doctor.question: Do you believe the voices you hear are the actual board members and staff, or do you think they might be impersonating them?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me through the conference room walls or from my phone even when it’s off, usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company, and it sounds so clear that I answer them before I realize no one else heard it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the nature of the voices the patient is hearing (whether they are the actual people or impersonators), which directly relates to the patient's hallucinations of hearing board members and staff talking about her.

patient.answer:
Impersonating them? No, no, it's definitely them. I know their voices. I mean, I hired most of them, didn't I? I hear them clear as day, right through the conference room walls, or—like I said—coming out of my phone when it's completely powered down. They're always saying the same things, that I'm ruining the company, that I don't know what I'm doing. It's so incredibly distinct that I'll literally answer them out loud. I'll be sitting there in my office, and I'll just say, "Excuse me, I can hear you," and then I realize the room is completely empty and no one else heard a thing. 

It's just like when I try to get a straight answer out of my interior designer, Marcus. I hired him to redo the executive suites, and I specifically asked for a minimalist aesthetic with cool tones. Slate grays, maybe a touch of navy. Do you know what he brought me? Swatches of mauve. Mauve! It's like a dusty purple from a 1980s waiting room. I told him, "Marcus, if I wanted my office to look like a discount dentist's lobby, I would have gone to a flea market." And he had the nerve to tell me that mauve is making a comeback. A comeback! Just like those high-waisted jeans everyone is wearing now. I tried a pair on at a boutique in SoHo last week, and I swear, the zipper went all the way up to my ribcage. Who finds that comfortable? You can't even sit down in them without feeling like you're being cut in half. I ended up just buying a cashmere wrap instead. You can never have too much cashmere, really. Though the dry cleaning bills are astronomical. My cleaner, Mr. Chen, he does a fabulous job, but he insists on using these wire hangers that just ruin the shoulders of my garments. I've told him a hundred times to use the velvet ones I provide, but he just smiles and nods and then—wire hangers. 

But yes, it's definitely the board members and the staff. I hear them talking about me ruining the company, and I answer them before I even realize they aren't actually in the room with me. It's them. I know it is.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's perception of the voices is related to their own self-criticism or fears
doctor.question: Do you think the voices you hear might be saying things that you, yourself, are afraid to admit or worry about?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me through the conference room walls or from my phone even when it’s off, usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company, and it sounds so clear that I answer them before I realize no one else heard it.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is probing whether the patient believes the voices she hears (hallucinations) might be a manifestation of her own internal fears or insecurities.

patient.answer:
Afraid to admit? No, I'm not afraid to admit anything. I'm a very straightforward person. That's why I'm here, actually. I came in because I keep hearing them—the board members, the staff—talking about me through the conference room walls, or from my phone even when it's completely off. They're always saying I'm ruining the company. And it sounds so incredibly clear that I answer them out loud before I even realize no one else heard it. 

It’s just like when I’m trying to order a simple salad at that new bistro downtown. You go in, and you just want a nice Niçoise, maybe some seared tuna, and they hand you a menu on an iPad. I don’t want to scroll through a digital interface to choose my dressing. And half the time, the screen is smudged with someone else's fingerprints. It’s incredibly unsanitary. I actually carry these little individually wrapped antibacterial wipes in my purse now. The lavender-scented ones. Though, honestly, the lavender is a bit overpowering. It smells less like a French countryside and more like a discount potpourri sachet you'd find in a grandmother's guest bathroom. I bought a real lavender plant for my kitchen windowsill hoping it would be better, but I think I overwatered it. Or maybe it didn't get enough sun? The lighting in my kitchen is very tricky. I had these imported Italian pendant lights installed, hand-blown glass, absolutely gorgeous, but the bulbs they require are nearly impossible to find. I had to order them from a specialty supplier in Milan, and they took six weeks to arrive. Six weeks! And when they finally got here, the delivery driver left the box right on the edge of the porch where it could have easily been knocked over by a stray cat. 

But no, I'm not worried about what they're saying. I just wish they would stop talking about me ruining the company when my phone is off.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's perception of the voices is related to their own self-criticism or fears
doctor.question: Do you think the voices might be echoing any criticisms you have of yourself?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me through the conference room walls or from my phone even when it’s off, usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company, and it sounds so clear that I answer them before I realize no one else heard it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the nature of the voices the patient hears, which is a manifestation of hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Criticisms of myself? No, I don't know why we keep going in circles about this. I'm not criticizing myself. Like I just explained to you, it's *them*. It's the board members and the staff. I hear them through the conference room walls, or coming out of my phone when it is completely powered down and sitting on my desk. They are the ones saying I’m ruining the company, not me. It sounds so real that I literally answer them out loud before I even realize the room is empty and nobody else heard it. 

I don't have time to sit around criticizing myself, I'm too busy trying to manage people who can't follow basic instructions. Take my assistant, Chloe, for example. I sent her out this morning to get me a simple iced matcha latte. I specifically said almond milk, light ice. She comes back twenty minutes later with oat milk. Oat milk! It tastes like liquid cardboard. I do not understand this obsession everyone has with oats right now. Overnight oats, oat milk, oat flour. It's peasant food. 

My grandmother used to feed oats to her horses. She had this stunning equestrian estate in Virginia, and we used to go riding every summer. I had a chestnut mare named Duchess. She was incredibly temperamental—you had to brush her coat exactly the way she liked, with this specific natural-bristle brush, or she'd try to nip at your fingers. I actually still have my custom leather riding boots from back then. They were handmade in Florence. The leather is so supple. It's not like the stiff, synthetic garbage they try to pass off as luxury these days. I went into a high-end boutique last week to look for some ankle boots, and the salesgirl actually tried to sell me "vegan leather." Vegan leather is just polyurethane! It's plastic! They slap a trendy, eco-friendly label on it and charge you eight hundred dollars. It's a complete scam. 

People just don't appreciate authenticity anymore. Which is exactly why I know I'm right about the business, despite what the board keeps whispering through the walls. I hear them clear as day. But no, to answer your question, it's not me criticizing myself. It's definitely them.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports hearing voices that are distinct, clear, and recognizable as specific individuals (board members and staff) criticizing their performance at work. These voices are not just thoughts or internal criticisms but are perceived as coming from outside the patient's mind, often through unusual means such as through conference room walls or from a powered-off phone. The patient's inability to recognize these voices as a product of their own mind, despite their content mirroring potential internal concerns or fears about work performance, aligns with the diagnostic criteria for persistent delusional disorders, specifically delusional disorder, persecutory type (F22).
